brief: UBS reads the recent chip selloff (Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down around 8% over five sessions, Kospi down over 12% since the start of October) as a reset in AI investment expectations rather than a deterioration, driven by doubts about AI spending durability, competition from China's rising memory maker, higher-for-longer rates, and OpenAI revenue-growth concerns that UBS says reflect accounting treatment rather than a drop in demand. Supporting UBS's constructive view: ASML raised its 2026 revenue forecast for a third straight quarter, S&P 500 EPS guidance sits at a five-year high with around 28% earnings growth expected, and semiconductor valuations remain below long-term averages even as financing costs, flagged by Broadcom's CEO, weigh on sentiment. UBS prefers the Magnificent 6 and semi-cap, robotics, foundry and OSAT names over memory. Separately, New York Fed President Williams said one more 2026 hike may be appropriate but none is needed in 2027, after which two-year yields edged lower; UBS expects a December hike rather than an October one, pending Wednesday's CPI. Singapore's MAS paused its tightening cycle; UBS still expects USDSGD to ease to 1.25.
